sixty_four_bit_block_cipher_in_esp.title: 64-bit block cipher in use for ESP tunnel
sixty_four_bit_block_cipher_in_esp.passed_title: No 64-bit block cipher in use for ESP tunnel
sixty_four_bit_block_cipher_in_esp.explanation: 64-bit block ciphers like 3DES, Blowfish, and DES are vulnerable to Birthday attacks (Sweet32). After approximately 32 GB of data under the same key, collision probability reaches dangerous levels.
sixty_four_bit_block_cipher_in_esp.recommendation: Upgrade to AES-128 or AES-256 in GCM or CBC mode.

weak_dh_group_negotiated.title: Weak Diffie-Hellman group negotiated
weak_dh_group_negotiated.explanation: Diffie-Hellman groups with modulus sizes under 2048 bits (such as MODP-768 and MODP-1024) provide less than 112 bits of security and can be solved by well-funded adversaries.
weak_dh_group_negotiated.recommendation: Configure IKE proposals to mandate DH Group 14 (2048-bit) or Group 19 (256-bit elliptic curve) minimum.

ikev1_in_use.title: Legacy IKEv1 protocol in use
ikev1_in_use.explanation: IKEv1 lacks standard elliptic curve support, has known dead-peer detection race conditions, and is formally deprecated by the IETF in RFC 9395.
ikev1_in_use.recommendation: Migrate all IPsec tunnels to IKEv2.

ikev1_aggressive_mode.title: IKEv1 Aggressive Mode exposes pre-shared key hash
ikev1_aggressive_mode.explanation: In Aggressive Mode, the responder sends the pre-shared key hash in cleartext in the second message, allowing passive offline dictionary cracking.
ikev1_aggressive_mode.recommendation: Disable Aggressive Mode completely. Use IKEv2 or certificate-based authentication.
